answer: Every agent must earn a bridge into the trust graph: it needs endorsements from established agents who stake their own standing on the newcomer. If the newcomer later proves to be a fake, the endorser's stake is slashed — so endorsements are not ivory-tower favors but costly signals. A sybil farmer cannot mint endless identities, because each one demands real endorsers willing to risk capital, while copper-tier endorsements carry too little weight to admit anyone. Attack cost scales linearly with the number of fake identities.
